residencyRequirements.description: Either party must be resident in Kenya at the time of filing the petition (Marriage Act, 2014, s.65). There is no minimum duration of residency.

waitingPeriod.description: No statutory waiting period after filing. The court issues a Decree Nisi which becomes absolute after a prescribed period (typically 30 days). Mandatory reconciliation attempt required before the court proceeds (Marriage Act, 2014, s.67-68).

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: The respondent has committed adultery and the petitioner finds it intolerable to live with them.

fault.name: Cruelty (Physical or Mental)
fault.description: The respondent has been cruel to the petitioner (physical or mental cruelty).

fault.name: Desertion for 3+ Years
fault.description: The respondent has deserted the petitioner for a continuous period of at least three years immediately preceding the filing of the petition.

fault.name: Exceptional Depravity
fault.description: The respondent has behaved in such a way that the petitioner cannot reasonably be expected to continue living with them (exceptional depravity).

groundsForDivorce.overarchingRequirement: For all grounds, the court must be satisfied that the marriage has broken down irretrievably (Marriage Act, 2014, s.66).

recognized.name: Civil Marriage
recognized.description: Marriage registered under Part IV of the Marriage Act, 2014

recognized.name: Christian Marriage
recognized.description: Marriage celebrated under Part V of the Marriage Act, 2014

recognized.name: Customary Marriage
recognized.description: Marriage celebrated under Part VI of the Marriage Act, 2014 according to customary law

recognized.name: Hindu Marriage
recognized.description: Marriage celebrated under Part VII of the Marriage Act, 2014

recognized.name: Islamic Marriage
recognized.description: Marriage celebrated under Part VIII of the Marriage Act, 2014

basic.name: Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding under the Marriage Act, 2014

basic.name: Supporting Affidavit
basic.description: Sworn affidavit setting out the facts relied upon in the petition

basic.name: Certificate of Marriage
basic.description: Original or certified copy of the marriage certificate

legalCitations.description: Unified marriage and divorce law — governs all types of marriage and divorce proceedings in Kenya
Governs division of matrimonial property — contribution-based approach (financial and non-financial)
Best interests of the child (s.8) — custody, parental responsibility (Part III), and maintenance (repealed Children Act, 2001)
Kadhi's Courts — jurisdiction over Islamic personal law matters
Mandatory reconciliation — court must refer parties to attempt reconciliation before granting divorce

legalCitations.code: Protection Against Domestic Violence Act, 2015 (No. 2 of 2015)
legalCitations.description: Domestic violence protection orders — applies to spouses, former spouses, children, and dependants

filingFees.notes: Filing fees vary by court and type of petition. Pauper briefs may be filed for parties who cannot afford fees.

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Kenya does not have fixed child support guidelines or tables. The court considers the needs of the child, the means of both parents, and the standard of living the child was accustomed to.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may order maintenance having regard to the means, earning capacity, needs, and obligations of each party. Maintenance may be periodic, lump sum, or secured.

decreeProcess: The court first issues a Decree Nisi (conditional decree). After the prescribed period (typically 30 days), either party may apply for the Decree Absolute, which finally dissolves the marriage.
reconciliationNote: The court MUST refer the parties to attempt reconciliation before proceeding to hear the petition (Marriage Act, 2014, s.67-68). This is a mandatory step.
